items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Britt Woodman even. ... And I think that’s one of the great things about these jazz parties. ... or Britt Woodman, they were always supportive of the younger cats.

ctx.x: Right. Who were your major trombone influences?

I know this doesn’t answer your question, I think my greatest influence was not a trombone player, it was Louis Armstrong actually. But guys that played with him. I’m often asked the question who is my favorite. I don’t really have one favorite because the trombone has many voices. And you have people like Jack Teagarden or Trummy Young, guys like Al Grey. Even guys like Frank Rosolino. A guy like Bill Watrous. I admired Bill Watrous for a long time. I got a chance to hear him when I was in high school and…

is categorized with the early New Orleans style or even a Dixieland style. I love J.J. Johnson. He’s great. He’s one of the cleanest trombone players ever. I love Curtis Fuller. I got a chance to work with him a couple of weeks ago. There are many. Major influences? I say guys like Lawrence Brown. He played the trombone like a trombone. He didn’t try to do the acrobatics of a saxophone or a trumpet. He played the trombone. He sang. He sang when he played. A lot of guys. Britt Woodman even. Some of the guys, well…
